Bring a job from another study into this one

Source: R/import-job.R
import_job.Rd

Copies a job .qmd from another study into the current study, keeping the source study's edits, so a job adapted once, such as an aorta-specific ac job, can be adapted again rather than rebuilt from the template.

Usage

import_job(from, subject = NULL, type = NULL, dir = NULL)

Arguments

from

The job to import: a .qmd file in another study, named as add_job() names jobs.

subject, type

The job's set in this study. NULL, the default, keeps the source job's. See add_job for what they decide.

dir

The study root to import into. NULL, the default, finds it by walking up from the working directory, as add_job() does.

Value

The imported job's path, invisibly. On any failure no file is left behind, the runner included.

Details

The job is written where add_job would write a new job from the same template, under the name it would give it, and with the same setup: the template's packages and any further packages the job's own setup chunk attaches are installed into the study's renv library, the Quarto provenance hooks are installed, and an existing job is never overwritten. The template is read from the job's file name, in either spelling add_job() has used.

subject and type default to the source job's own. Either can be changed on the way in, and the job's SUBJECT and TYPE lines are rewritten to match its new name, as add_job() does.

A job that runs from a companion runner script brings its runner too, when one sits beside it. Without one, the job gets the template's runner, and the message says so.

What to review. Everything else is carried as the source study left it, including choices that were right for that study and may be wrong for this one. import_job() rewrites none of them. Instead its message lists, by line number, each one to check:

  • the DATASET the job reads;

  • a WHERE row selection, unless it is NULL;

  • every EDIT: marker still in the job;

  • every absolute file path, such as "/studies/aorta/..." or "C:/...", which names a file in the other study or on another machine.

Values are never quoted in the message, because a selection can name a patient. Paths relative to the study, which is how a template refers to its study's files, are not listed.

The job keeps the template version it was written from, so upgrade_job can bring an older job up to the current template afterwards: upgrade_job(import_job(from)).

See also

add_job, upgrade_job

Examples

other <- file.path(tempdir(), "import-job-other")
here <- file.path(tempdir(), "import-job-here")
for (d in c(other, here)) {
  invisible(hvtiRutilities::study_setup(d, study = "Example", study_tracker_id = 1L, renv = FALSE))
}
job <- add_job("ac", subject = "death", type = "hz", dir = other)
# The other study's edit.
lines <- readLines(job)
lines <- sub("^DATASET <- \"built\"", "DATASET <- \"built_aorta\"", lines)
writeLines(lines, job)

imported <- import_job(job, subject = "reop", dir = here)
#> import_job(): wrote '/tmp/RtmpHRw3ti/import-job-here/20_distributions/ac.reop.hz.qmd' from '/tmp/RtmpHRw3ti/import-job-other/20_distributions/ac.death.hz.qmd'.
#> Review in ac.reop.hz.qmd:
#>   DATASET: line 117
#>   EDIT: markers: lines 33, 116, 119, 122, 127, 132, 157, 162
grep("^(DATASET|SUBJECT) ", readLines(imported), value = TRUE)
#> [1] "SUBJECT <- \"reop\""        "DATASET <- \"built_aorta\""

# An existing job is never overwritten.
try(import_job(job, subject = "reop", dir = here))
#> Error : import_job(): '/tmp/RtmpHRw3ti/import-job-here/20_distributions/ac.reop.hz.qmd' already exists; refusing to overwrite.
unlink(c(other, here), recursive = TRUE)
